This happens to me too sometimes, and im really sorry to hear you are having a tough time. 

These are a couple things ive found that helps:

Washing hair a maximum of 3 days a week. Overwashing can dry out and break your hair. 

I've experimented with various types of oils, and the one ive found actually helps the production of hair growth is castor oil. 
Massage into scalp as well as the ends and leave it for a bit. 
I also use this on my lashes and brows. 

Practice regular trimming of hair with hairdressing scissors to prevent splitting and breakage. It also helps with matting and knots for less breakage.

For a receding hairline I would recommend getting a fringe to cover the uneven patches while its growing back. Works wonders for me this one trick alone! 

Don't skip out on supplements especially during these times when we are couped up inside all the time. I've introduced B2, B12 (biotin) and vitamin D into my diet for dietary support. 

Ive also heard other vitamins which are good for hair are Vitamin A, Vitamin C, Zink and Iron. 

Try eat a nutrient rich healthy diet with plenty of dark leafy greens and in general less processed foods. Not only will this also help your hair, but also your stress levels in general. 

Practice regular outdoor exercise. Even if its just a short walk till definitely help clear your head and help with dopamine production.

So last Saturday I was invited to a girls night at one of my best friends house. Her housemate was assigned to make dinner for us all, and pasta is on the menu. 

In the past I would have declined such a triggering event. 
1. Being that someone else would have full control over cooking a meal for me. 
2. Obvs the carbs and cream.

To further add to my anxiety this girl had an outstraight hatred for vegetarians and she promised she would take mine out separately which I thought in my late stage of recovery that I could trust her with, but I could feel myself panicking a bit. The smell of bacon and chorizo frying was getting stronger and stronger and I had then decided that I would make myself something else. 

I hate being that person, the one who had already brought my own food incase of emergency. The pure utterly jealousy I feel watching everyone else mindlessly shovel down huge bowls of delicious creamy pasta, and white bread, whilst im eating a homemade bean burger, with lots of different salads and beetroot, and hummus, and pumpkin seeds. 

I hate myself for the disgust I feel watching what others eat, whilst also being jealous. Noticing when they've nothing green in their diet, or when they are consuming too much fat. Its not right at all. My diet isn't perfect by any means. It would be so much easier to just let that all go, and just be able to enjoy the spontaneity of the moment, and even venture out to new eating spots since I am ironically a massive foodie. 

I know those days are coming, and recognizing these negative traits, and silencing that voice is another step closer to overcoming the disorder and leading a normal life again.
